newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up on good sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up on good sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up on Monday on good sentiment following overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange, but off highs due to fresh selling and profit-taking, traders said.
The most active May 1997 contract ended at an intraday low of 23,380 yuan ($2,819) per tonne, up 70 yuan on the previous close. It opened up at 23,500 and hit a high of 23,600.
March rose 210 yuan to 23,160, April 130 to 23,310, June 80 to 23,380, July 90 to 23,390 and August 100 to 23,400.
Combined volume rose sharply to 94,470 tonnes from 35,370.
Copper opened higher and rose further before fresh selling and profit-taking emerged, pushing most contracts down to near their intraday lows.
"The LME gains boosted the confidence of long-position holders, resulting in continued rises on the Shanghai copper market," one trader said.
"But the market risks increased after heavy gains," another trader said. "Open interest rose sharply on Monday, indicating some investors built short positions at high levels."
Traders said investors were cautious about buying at high levels, which is likely to bring a short-term correction.
"Upward potential will be limited due to a lack of follow-up buying, but sharp falls are impossible due to the strong movement on the LME," a second trader said.
Analysts said they expected copper to be firm in the mid- term despite the short-term technical correction.
Aluminium followed copper's trend. March rose 160 yuan to 15,630 per tonne, April 120 to 15,920, May 220 to 16,220 and June 130 to 16,230.
Combined volume rose to 1,500 tonnes from 150.
